spans.text: Several hours earlier, inside a hotel suite.
By the window, through the thick pane of glass, the Commander's gaze locks onto William's figure. William steps out of the hotel and walks toward the motorcade waiting for him.
As if sensing the stare, he turns and looks directly toward the Commander's position. After a brief pause, he gets into the car.
The convoy starts up and disappears into the city lights. The Commander picks up the communicator on the table and presses a contact to dial—
Click!
All the lights in the room suddenly go out. The abrupt darkness swallows their vision.
The Commander then hears a faint sound stir behind them.
Slash!
A flash of cold steel cuts through the dark. The Commander rolls aside at once, narrowly avoiding the blade.
The shadow gripping the weapon presses the attack without hesitation. The knife plunges into the Commander's left shoulder.
Ugh...!
The instant the cold metal pulls free, searing pain surges through their body like wildfire.
The Commander tenses their muscles and slams their weight into the attacker before the blade can strike again, forcing them back.
Huff... huff...
Cold sweat beads on their forehead. The pain in their left shoulder makes every breath excruciating.
Darkness obstructs their sight like a thick veil, but they can hear the attacker's heavy breathing.
There is no time to think. The attacker charges again.
The Commander rolls sideways. The blade whistles past, grazing the back of their neck and slicing through their collar.
The shriek of steel cutting cloth makes their scalp prickle.
Their injured shoulder slams against the carpet mid-roll, fresh agony causing their eyes to water.
Instinct overrides pain. Relying on memory of the room's layout, they duck behind the sofa.
Almost simultaneously, the dagger buries itself into the upholstery with a dull thud.
That's my chance...!
As the attacker wrenches the knife free, the Commander lunges up and sweeps their right leg toward the sound.
A solid impact. Their kick connects with the attacker's neck.
...Ugh!
The muffled cry reveals something unexpected—this attacker is a woman.
Bastard...
Even so, her strength is formidable, and her assault grows more frenzied.
The blade carves wildly through the dark, narrowly skimming their ribs and waist.
The Commander can only take advantage of nearby furniture to block and counter. Each exertion tears at the wound in their shoulder, causing blood to gush steadily.
Huff... huff...
They're reaching their limit. Their movements slow.
Her attacks only grow sharper. Blow by blow, they're driven into the corner of the room.
The Commander is not oblivious to their predicament.
Thud!
When their back slams against the wall, they know that they've run out of room to retreat.
...Ugh.
Sweat has soaked their clothes. The blood loss is making the world spin. Even standing upright becomes difficult.
She senses the opening. The knife point whistles forward through the darkness.
Crap...!
Clang!
Steel strikes something impossibly hard, sending bright sparks flying in the dark.
In that split-second glow, the Commander glimpses a tall figure.
...Hnng!!!
The attacker only realizes someone else is also in the suite when a hand clamps around her throat.
She hacks at the arm restraining her, but her ferocious attacks don't seem to present any threat against the newcomer.
Each strike hits as though against solid iron, throwing up sparks again and again—illuminating a familiar face.
The sparks fade. The blade wavers.
AK-15 moves.
Her fingers tighten, and the attacker's throat feels as if crushed by a hydraulic press.
Cough... Ack!
Overwhelmed by absolute strength, the woman drops her knife and claws at AK-15's grip, futilely trying to pry free.
AK-15 raises her arm, lifting the attacker like a toy, legs kicking uselessly in midair.
Ro...bin...
The Commander's pupils constrict violently.
Hmph.
AK-15 gives the attacker no chance for further struggle. She pivots and hurls her across the room.
Thunk!
Her body slams into the wall.
Before she falls to the floor, AK-15 closes in and drives a kick like a cannon shot straight into her throat—
Crack!!!
In the silent room, the sound of bone snapping is unmistakable.
The attacker who had moments ago assaulted the Commander so fiercely is now pinned to the wall by AK-15's single leg, motionless.
With the danger passed, the Commander's legs give out.
As they collapse, another pair of arms catches them gently.
The Commander can tell that they're being administered swift first-aid treatment. Long, soft hair brushes across their face, carrying a faint fragrance.
They raise a hand weakly, but grasp only empty air—until the person guides it softly to her cheek.
The curtains are drawn open again.
The Commander gets a good look at her.
Commander...!
Wasting no further words, AN-94 focuses on treating their wound, then helps them over to the sofa.
Across the room, AK-15 lowers her foot. The corpse of the hotel attendant drops halfway, then halts midair.
AK-12 deactivates her invisibility and gently sets the body down.
The lights come back on. The Commander finally sees the attacker's true face.
Tsk...
Even AK-12 finds herself momentarily speechless.
I've never met her in person, but this doesn't look like the Morridow I know...
I gather this must be...?
...She's no one.
Just a Nyto.
The Commander stares wordlessly at that familiar face.
Once life fades completely, the features lose coherence, dissolving until they become unrecognizable.
Instead of killing me, he wants to see me consumed by rage, frantic and hysterical.
The same way he lost his composure in front of me.
AK-15 retrieves the communicator from the floor.
Your communicator.
Thank you. Good thing you were here. You ended it in an instant.
...It could have been even faster.
What do you mean by that?
Nele found an interesting blueprint among Doctor Shaw's legacy—a fully wearable combat exoskeleton.
If 15 had that suit, this opponent would've been completely vaporized.
Unfortunately, at this stage it's still only a design on paper, so it obviously didn't turn out that way.
...It would be useful.
I see.
Even Nele thinks it would be extremely difficult to realize the design.
It's probably just one of the Doctor's usual flights of fancy. She had them quite often.
Knock, knock, knock.
Commander, was there a disturbance in your suite?
No, I just popped open a bottle of red wine.
...Understood.
If you require assistance, please let us know.
Sure.
Only after silence settles outside does AK-15 lower her weapon from the door.
How is it?
The body has all but dissolved. No clue what lab results would say about the residual tissue...
But it likely won't serve as evidence against anyone. As you said, this was premeditated.
Are you really alright?
AN-94 sounds concerned, but the Commander simply shrugs.
Machlian is dead. I buried her myself.
But her spirit lives on in my memory and will not be replaced by any imitation.
If William thinks this will shake me, then he underestimates me.
Was it really necessary to provoke him to this extent?
As I said, we confirmed it was definitely him earlier. We could've struck directly.
No.
The Commander shakes their head.
Killing William may satisfy our desire for revenge, but it achieves nothing more.
Nele killed Capita, yet William still inherited her research.
What we must destroy is not a man named William, but the force he represents.
That force stands under the protection of the Earl. So we must first uncover it.
The more mistakes William makes, the better our chances of digging out his foundation...
...He has begun to slip, but it is far from enough.
I will kill him—to avenge Ange, Machlian, and the countless innocent lives he has ruined.
But I must also completely eliminate the possibility of the Earl—or anyone else—exploiting this heinous research.
Mm, that's the spirit.
Just give the word.
Whatever decision you make, Task Force DEFY will follow.
...Thank you.
Still... you should've contacted us sooner. Then you wouldn't have been hurt so badly...
He was probing me, just as I was probing him. I had to accept the risk that came with it.
At least now I can be certain that we have come to a consensus on one point...
We both want the other dead. And to achieve that, neither of us wants the Earl to interfere.
From here on, unless absolutely necessary, our actions cannot violate that principle. Otherwise, we lose all opportunities.
That is why I came here.
And why I needed... external assistance.
Speaking of which, Beluga's last attempt failed.
So she has decided to try your method... What are your thoughts? Personally, I think she's a ticking time bomb.
It's fine. That was accounted for.
Just pass on my request.
I knew you had another card up your sleeve, Commander.
The Commander lowers their head and falls silent for a moment. Then they shake their head with a wan smile.
I did not expect Tokarev, C14, Six12, and CZ-805 to be dragged into this...
I hope my friend has retrieved their neural cores as agreed.
Your friend... Then the one who contacted us is...?
Hmph... Who else could it be?
The Commander says nothing further. They glance at the clock, then at the communicator on the table.
Beep-beep!
Two minutes later, it rings.
Seeing the confusion on 94's and 15's faces, the Commander answers.
How could you ever doubt my efficiency, Commander...? You wound me~
Of course I retrieved their neural cores. Sheesh, I can't believe that old man let them in.
If he had detained them at the door, there would have been no need for this extra trouble. Once those autonomous Dolls activate, there's no stopping them.
The voice on the other end is unmistakably familiar.
The Commander cannot help but shake their head.
Enough theatrics. It is time to move on to the next stage...
Dandelion.
